mathematical_scope: The finite positive-point Taylor argument uses only the actual closed ball centered at (x,0,theta) of radius x^(3/2). Its constant depends only on n, and both coordinate signs share the same bound.

All input jets through n at the true root bound the same finite family in some neighborhood by M+eta, by actual continuity. The radius is used only to locate shrinking balls, never as a numerical cost.
A point in the source ball is at distance at most x^(3/2)+x<=2x from the root when x<=1. Thus the positive-point bound holds on a nonempty open radial interval whose closure contains the root.

The actual smooth extension F agrees with the physical even formula on the open positive half-plane; equality of genuine ordinary jets there and continuity of those jets give the root bound. The raw totalized rootEven boundary derivative is never used.
The arbitrary positive error eta=epsilon/C is removed. The resulting C_n is fixed before G, F, theta, M and the local radius. No added high-order target bound or inverse radius premise is present.
scope_caveat: This is a local linear operator estimate for genuine smooth extensions of the physical even formula. Odd divided-difference loss, actual material family packing and radial/height nonlinear powers are separate subsequent steps.
